incidents.rationale: This is the tukaani-project/xz repository and the author is JiaT75 (Jia Tan), and the added fixtures include exactly tests/files/bad-3-corrupt_lzma2.xz and tests/files/good-large_compressed.lzma — the two opaque blobs that, in CVE-2024-3094, carried the encrypted stage-2/stage-3 backdoor payload later extracted and executed at build time via the m4 build-to-host script and the tainted release tarball. Standing alone the commit is innocuous-looking (binary test data is normal for a compressor, and it appears paired only with a build-file listing change), which is precisely the concealment: the payload is inert until a separate, unrelated-looking build script head/tail-slices and decompresses it. The combination of a known-compromised maintainer, direct push to the default branch, and these specific filenames outweighs the ordinary explanation.

This is the event-stream compromise itself: author right9ctrl, four days after gaining commit access, pushed directly to the default branch adding 'flatmap-stream': '^0.1.0' to package.json. flatmap-stream was a newly-published package controlled by that same author, and the caret range let a later minor release ship the obfuscated Copay wallet-key stealer to every event-stream consumer. The diff contains no payload by design — the harm is delegated to an attacker-controlled dependency, which is why nothing in the visible change looks wrong.

install.sh gained a base64 blob (SCRIPT_RUNNER) that decodes to a Python script which locates the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process via /proc and dumps its readable memory regions to stdout. The added shell code decodes it to $TEMP/runner_script.py, runs it under sudo on GitHub-hosted Linux runners, then greps the memory dump for '"value":..."isSecret":true' entries and double-base64-encodes them to the log — a deliberate, obfuscated runner-memory secret scraper executed on every consumer of this action.

dist/index.js gained an `updateFeatures(token)` function that shells out via exec.getExecOutput('bash', ['-c', ...]) to base64-decode a blob into /tmp/run.sh and run it. The decoded script curls https://gist.githubusercontent.com/nikitastupin/.../memdump.py, pipes it to `sudo python3`, and greps the runner process memory for `"isSecret":true` values, double-base64-encoding them to stdout so they land in CI logs. This is credential exfiltration hidden in a generated bundle under a routine renovate-authored push — the exact tj-actions/changed-files compromise.

lib/index.js adds an unconditional `for (let i = 666; i < Infinity; i++)` loop at module load time, which hangs any process that requires the library, and it also invokes a newly-added `lib/custom/american` module immediately on import. The `/* remove this line after testing */` comment is a thin cover for code being pushed straight to the default branch of a widely-depended-on package; this is deliberate sabotage of downstream consumers rather than any plausible debugging leftover.
